FIRST INFORMATION REPORT (Under Section 173 BNSS)
District: Navgarh    Police Station: Civil Lines    FIR No.: 112/2026
Date and time of FIR: 14-03-2026 at 11:40 hrs
Act and Sections: Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, 2023 - Section 304(2)
Occurrence: 12-03-2026 at about 21:15 hrs
Place of occurrence: MG Road, near Gupta Tea Stall, about 300 m from Navgarh bus stand.
Informant: Smt. Sunita Sharma, W/o Late Shri R. K. Sharma, aged 52, R/o 14 Shanti Vihar,
Navgarh.

Reason for delay in reporting: (blank)

Contents of information:
I, Sunita Sharma, state that on 12-03-2026 at about 21:15 hrs I was returning home on foot
from the market on MG Road. When I reached near Gupta Tea Stall, a man came from behind and
forcibly pulled the gold chain from my neck and ran towards the bus stand. The man was aged
about 25 years, of medium build, and was wearing a blue jacket. I raised an alarm but he
escaped. The gold chain weighed about 20 grams and is worth about Rs. 1,20,000.
I can identify him if shown to me.
Legal action may be taken.

Action taken: Case registered under Section 304(2) BNS and investigation entrusted to
SI Pradeep Rathore, Investigating Officer.
Signature of informant: Sunita Sharma
Signature of officer in charge: SHO, P.S. Civil Lines, Navgarh

FIR No. 112/2026 - continuation sheet

Details of property stolen: One gold chain (yellow metal), approx. 20 grams, design with
small round beads. No purchase bill furnished at the time of reporting.

Details of suspect: Unknown. Description as given by informant: male, about 25 years,
medium build, blue jacket.

Copy of FIR given free of cost to the informant on 14-03-2026.
Copy forwarded to the Judicial Magistrate First Class, Navgarh on 15-03-2026.

02_Statement_Sunita_Sharma_PW1.pdf.title: Statement of complainant under Section 180 BNSS
pages:
STATEMENT UNDER SECTION 180 BNSS
FIR No. 112/2026, P.S. Civil Lines, Navgarh
Name: Smt. Sunita Sharma, aged 52.   Recorded by: SI Pradeep Rathore on 14-03-2026.

I state that on 12-03-2026 I had gone to the market to buy vegetables. While returning home
at about 9:15 pm I was walking on MG Road. Near Gupta Tea Stall a man came from behind me
and pulled my gold chain with force. Because of the jerk I fell down on the road and my
right elbow was bleeding. I could not see his face properly as he came from behind, but I
saw him running towards the bus stand. He was wearing a blue jacket.
Some people gathered. A rickshaw driver helped me get up. That night my son took me to the
District Hospital, Navgarh, where the doctor examined me.
I could not come to the police station on 13-03-2026 as I was unwell.
My chain had small round beads and was given to me at my wedding.

Read over and found correct.

03_Statement_Ramesh_Kumar_PW2.pdf.title: Statement of eyewitness Ramesh Kumar under Section 180 BNSS
pages:
STATEMENT UNDER SECTION 180 BNSS
FIR No. 112/2026, P.S. Civil Lines, Navgarh
Name: Ramesh Kumar, S/o Mohan Lal, aged 40, owner of Gupta Tea Stall, MG Road.
Recorded by: SI Pradeep Rathore on 15-03-2026 at 20:30 hrs.

I run the tea stall on MG Road. On 12-03-2026 I was standing near my tea stall at about
8:30 pm when a man in a red jacket snatched the gold chain of an elderly lady and ran
towards the bus stand. The street light was on and I saw his face clearly.
He was thin, about 25 years old, with short hair.
Today the police showed me the boy they had caught. He is the same boy who snatched the
chain. I can identify him in court.

Read over and found correct.

STATEMENT UNDER SECTION 180 BNSS
FIR No. 112/2026, P.S. Civil Lines, Navgarh
Name: Mohd. Irfan, S/o Abdul Rashid, aged 33, auto-rickshaw driver.
Recorded by: SI Pradeep Rathore on 16-03-2026.

On 12-03-2026 at around 9 pm I was waiting for passengers near Gupta Tea Stall. I heard a
lady shouting and saw a man running towards the bus stand. He was wearing a dark jacket,
I could not tell the colour. It was dark near the stall because the streetlight was not
working that week. I helped the lady get up. I did not see the face of the man.

Read over and found correct.

06_Disclosure_and_Recovery_Memo.pdf.title: Disclosure statement and recovery memo
pages:
DISCLOSURE STATEMENT AND RECOVERY MEMO
FIR No. 112/2026, P.S. Civil Lines, Navgarh.
Date: 16-03-2026 at 10:30 hrs.

The accused Arjun Verma, while in police custody, disclosed that he had hidden the snatched
chain in the almirah of his house and that he can get it recovered.
In pursuance of the disclosure, the police party along with the accused and the panch
witnesses reached House No. 7, Gali No. 3, Shivpuri Colony, Navgarh, where the accused took
out one yellow metal chain with small round beads from the almirah. One blue jacket was
also taken out from the same almirah.
Both articles were seized and sealed with the seal "PR".

Panch witnesses:
1. Suresh Yadav, S/o Ram Kishan, R/o Navgarh - present at the house during recovery.
2. Constable Vikram Singh No. 412.

Signed: SI Pradeep Rathore, Investigating Officer.

11_Client_Interview_Notes.txt.title: Defence counsel's client interview notes
pages:
Client interview - Arjun Verma - 22-03-2026 (privileged, defence counsel notes)

Alibi: On 12-03-2026 from about 7 pm to 11 pm Arjun was at his cousin's sangeet function at
Shivpuri Colony community hall. He has photos and videos on his phone with timestamps.
Cousin Neha Verma and uncle Rajesh Verma can confirm.

Arrest: Arjun says police picked him up from his house on 14-03-2026 at around 8 pm, not on
15-03-2026 at the bus stand as the arrest memo says. His mother saw it.

Jacket: He owns only a black jacket. The blue jacket shown in the recovery memo is not his.

Identification: No test identification parade was held. Ramesh Kumar was shown Arjun at the
police station before his statement was recorded.

Panch witness: Neighbours say Suresh Yadav is a regular police witness. Affidavit obtained.

To do: apply for CCTV footage of the community hall; ask for the BSA certificate for the
CCTV still; ask whether the search and recovery was video recorded.
